proposal.reason: Trial 1 is a regularized logistic baseline on one-hot categories with modest accuracy and imbalanced class recall. A CatBoost model with native categorical handling is a reasonable next primary-split candidate to test whether nonlinear feature interactions improve accuracy.
proposal.review: Only one completed primary trial exists: logistic_C0.05 with search accuracy 0.6747, train accuracy 0.6799, and a small score gap. The logistic route remains active; catboost, extra_trees, and field_interactions are untried. No confirmation-split comparison is available.
proposal.hypothesis: A depth-6 CatBoost classifier using native categorical representations may capture interactions that the one-hot logistic baseline misses, potentially increasing primary-split accuracy.
proposal.uncertainty: There is only one baseline trial, so the direction and magnitude of change are unknown. The nonlinear route is untested here, class recall is imbalanced, and categorical cardinality/interaction effects are not yet observed. This candidate is exploratory and may not improve accuracy.
